analysis.investment_thesis: CSB Bank is explicitly excluded from my Magic Formula — financial companies distort both EBIT/EV and ROIC calculations. Even applying bank-adapted metrics (ROE as ROIC proxy, earnings yield via P/E), the numbers disappoint: ROE of 13.2% falls well short of my 20%+ hurdle, and net profit CAGR of just 9% against 33.8% surging finance costs signals accelerating NIM compression that will erode future returns.
key_strengths: Reasonable valuation: forward P/E of 7.86 implies ~12.7% earnings yield — the cheapness side of the formula clears the 12% bar
Revenue growing at 20.5% CAGR (2022–2025), showing genuine loan book expansion
Solid promoter holding (40%) with FII + DII together at 28%, indicating institutional confidence
key_risks: Finance costs exploding at 33.8% CAGR vs. 20.5% revenue growth — cost of funds is outrunning income, compressing margins structurally
Free cash flow collapsed to -5,556 Cr in FY2025 and OCF positive only 2 of 4 years — earnings are not converting to cash
Net profit growth decelerating sharply: 9% CAGR vs. 20.5% revenue CAGR means the bank is working harder for less
red_flags: BANK — categorically excluded from Magic Formula; EBIT/EV and ROIC are meaningless metrics here
Finance cost CAGR (33.8%) > Revenue CAGR (20.5%) — funding costs are eating the business alive
FCF -5,556 Cr in FY2025 after +1,665 Cr in FY2024 — violent cash flow swings signal balance sheet stress, not operating strength
Debt surged from 1,757 Cr to 5,246 Cr in a single year (FY2024→FY2025) — 3x increase demands explanation
analysis.detailed_analysis:
My Magic Formula cannot be applied to CSB Bank — I explicitly exclude all financial companies because customer deposits masquerade as debt, destroying enterprise value calculations, and 'capital' in a bank has nothing to do with net working capital plus fixed assets. Forcing the formula here would produce nonsense. Adapting to bank-relevant metrics: ROE of 13.2% is the closest proxy for return on capital, and it fails my 20% hurdle outright. This is a mediocre-quality business at a modestly cheap price — the worst outcome from a Magic Formula lens (cheap AND bad).

The deteriorating economics are the real story. Revenue grew 20.5% CAGR but net profit only 9% — the gap is entirely explained by finance costs compounding at 33.8%. The bank is funding growth with expensive liabilities, and profitability is being squeezed. The FY2025 OCF of -5,256 Cr (after +1,783 Cr in FY2024) is a serious warning sign. On the quality-vs-price matrix, this stock scores on neither dimension that matters to me: quality is sub-threshold, and cheapness alone never wins the formula.
